constraint_findings.finding: The MOV clamp is SOURCED at 395 V max, but only at the datasheet's IPK=50 A, 8/20 us test current. The provisional product surge current (500 A L-L prospective) is 10x higher, and the clamp is untabulated there, so 395 V is a LOWER BOUND on the surge terminal voltage.
At 395 V the active-bridge MOSFET's 600 V class has 1.52x; at the true surge clamp the margin is unknown and strictly smaller (1.00x at 600 V, 1.20x at 500 V).

The TEA2209T L/R/VR and differential nodes sit at 0.898 of their 440 V OPERATING limit at the sourced clamp. If the surge clamp exceeds 440 V they exceed the operating limit during the surge (transient limit 700 V still applies).
The controller's 700 V transient limit is NOT a MOSFET requirement; a higher-rated MOSFET does not lower the node voltage.
The surge contract (IEC 61000-4-5, 1 kV L-L / 2 kV L-PE) is PROVISIONAL/ASSUMED; no committed requirement document names it.
The L-N MOV does not clamp the L-PE common-mode surge; controller/bridge common-mode stress is INDETERMINATE.
A line-surge MOV does not resolve the internally powered boost-switch-short capacitor-discharge fault; that loop is AR-PROTECT's question.

answer: CAPTURED and CONDITIONAL. The V150LA10AP clamp is 395 V MAXIMUM at IPK = 50 A, 8/20 us (Littelfuse LA Series datasheet, Rev VL 16/9/2024, page 2); rating basis ITM 4500 A 8/20 us and WTM 45 J 10/1000 us. This replaces AR-VERIFY's ASSUMED ~400 V with a sourced number. Derived from 395 V: the off active-bridge MOSFET needs a blocking rating above the clamped terminal voltage, giving 1.52x on a 600 V class; the TEA2209T's L/R/VR (and VCCHL/VCCHR/gate, dV(VR-L)/dV(VR-R)) nodes sit at 0.898 of their 440 V operating limit and 0.564 of their 700 V transient limit. BUT the datasheet guarantees the clamp only at 50 A while the provisional contract's prospective L-L surge current is 500 A, where the clamp is higher and untabulated: 395 V is a LOWER BOUND and the real margins are smaller (the controller may exceed its 440 V operating limit during the surge). The IEC 61000-4-5 1 kV/2 kV contract remains PROVISIONAL/ASSUMED. A line-surge MOV does not resolve the internally powered discharge loop, which stays AR-PROTECT's question.

single_missing_input.input: The V150LA10AP clamp voltage at the ACTUAL MOV current of the surge event - i.e. a captured/measured 8/20 us V-I characteristic read at the MOV's operating current (hundreds of A), not the datasheet's 50 A test point - under a COMMITTED surge requirement.
single_missing_input.why: The sourced 395 V is a lower bound; every derived margin (MOSFET rating, controller node stress) is one-sided until the clamp at the real current is known. It is the one number that can move the 600 V device from adequate to insufficient and the controller from within to above its 440 V operating limit.
